Definition: properly, a cord (as twisted), i.e. (by implication) a boundary; by extension the territory inclosed
BiblicalUsage: gᵉbûwl — border, territory. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 196 occurrences, and in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: What gᵉbûwl tells me is that God sets boundaries, and His boundaries are for our good. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
RelatedEvents: The Plague of Frogs; Edom Refuses Israel Passage; The Defeat of Sihon and Og
